title: Maxey's two terms at Angola and parole
summary: Maxey says this is his second time at Angola; first sentence 1949 to 1956, then parole, and a new sentence.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: I'm just wondering, now, this is your first time in Angola?
This is my second time in Angola.
Did you see many changes in the two different towns?

Well, I have. I've seen the right smile to change in the two times that I have been here. However, I have never been free from this place since I've been here. I have never been a free man since I first come to this institution.
When did you first come in?
And that was your first sentence? When was that through?
Well, that would be through in June of 27, 1956.
Well, I left here on parole, and I got out and brought more time back here with me. So I've been here now ever since.
How long did you get out on parole?

I stayed out on parole three years. And I've been back here now, soon be five years. And I've seen quite a lot of difference from the first time I was here up until now. So there's been lots of change I've made in the institution since I first come here.
